source.unit: Meteorology I.9, entire chapter between Part9 andPart10.
source.checked: E.W.Webster English translation read at MIT.
source.content: Solar heat raises moisture; cooling returns it as water. Cloud, residual mist, drizzle and rain receive distinct roles within the cycle, with an Oceanus interpretation offered speculatively.

design.whole_passage_relation: A full account covers region/cause, ascent, loss of heat, condensation, descent, recurrence, residual mist and precipitation-size distinction; the optional Oceanus claim stays attributed as speculation.
two_reused_input_cases: The same moisture changes from rising vapour to descending water, preserving material reference.
Cloud yielding precipitation versus remaining mist gives different outcomes under related phase vocabulary.
design.rival: Water already present is pumped through a vessel network, with no phase transformation or solar guard.
design.distinct_consequence: A real phase transition requires substance/state continuity and changes the applicability of later operations; container filling is not BECOMES_WATER.
design.falsifier: Fail if the fixed complete reading needs a vessel to become its contents, omits mist to preserve a two-state story, or uses one verb as both containment and phase change without a construction.
design.smallest_step: Author all source obligations as a linked graph and whole target passage sequence; compare phase-change and hydraulic rivals under unchanged repeated forms.
new_costs: Material identity through phase changes is explicit; no rates, temperatures or modern hydrological mass equation.
Source hypothetical etymology is not certain narrative fact.
predecessors: GDT817 retains chedy=BECOMES doublet conflict and no portable condensation clause. None of its glosses are inherited; exact whole-cycle content is the changed input.
design.main_gap: No target phase nouns or predicates are bound; source completeness may exceed the available target without unjustified compression.
